To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ER is a highly dynamic organelle that is capable of rapidly altering the composition of its membrane and lumen in response to cellular signals, and that this is achieved through a combination of regulated transport and membrane contact sites.

(i) the endoplasmic-reticulum-associated membrane protein (ERAMP) family of proteins are ER-membrane tether proteins that are required for the localization of the ER-mitochondria encounter structure (ERMES) complex to mitochondria, and (ii) ERAMPs are required for efficient calcium signalling and phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PI4P) production at the mitochondria-endoplasmic reticular contact sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of ER membrane contact sites in regulating cellular calcium and phosphoinositol signalling, which are critical for cellular homeostasis and survival.
understanding the role of membrane contact sites in the regulation of ER calcium and phosphoinositiides, and how defects in these processes contribute to human disease.
the molecular mechanisms of membrane contact sites and the roles of these membrane junctions in cellular physiology and pathology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
membrane contact sites are a key component of the ER, which plays a major role in the regulation of calcium and phospholipid metabolism.
we have a good idea of what we do not know about these membrane contact sites, and a growing list of what we do know.
the membrane contact sites of the ER are essential for the maintenance of cellular homeostasis and the coordination of cellular signalling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ER is an organelle with a highly dynamic structure that is able to adapt to changing cellular conditions.
membrane contact sites provide a mechanism to regulate calcium and phosphoinositiides at the ER membrane.
the ER is a central player in cellular signalling, but that it is not the only player.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ER's ability to form membrane contact sites with other organelles allows the ER to serve as a hub for cellular signalling and regulation.
ER-membrane contact sites are not just static structures but are dynamic and regulated, with the capacity to respond to changes in the cellular environment.
the ER is not a passive store of calcium or a phosphoinositide sink, but a dynamic organelle that actively regulates calcium signalling and phospholipid metabolism.
